title: A new class of antibiotic candidates against MRSA
summary: A deep-learning model trained on about 39,000 compounds screened about 12 million commercial compounds; of about 280 purchased and tested, two from the same class reduced MRSA burden tenfold in two mouse models, with very low toxicity to human cells. Results from plates and mice; toxicity was partly predicted computationally.

evidence.tested: About 283 compounds were bought and tested empirically; one structural class reduced bacterial burden in mouse skin and systemic thigh infection models, and cytotoxicity to human cells was measured.
evidence.unknown: The page does not list specific study limitations; next steps are chemical property analysis and potential clinical use.
evidence.ai_role: Graph neural network ensembles trained on about 39,000 compounds with measured antibacterial and human-cell toxicity predicted both properties for about 12 million compounds and flagged candidates for purchase and testing.
